t: A principality created in 1719 when the Liechtenstein family united Vaduz and Schellenberg to gain a seat in the Imperial Diet.
It outlived the Holy Roman Empire and the German Confederation, abolished its army in 1868 and tied itself to Switzerland in 1923.
A microstate of about 40,000 people, it combines strong princely powers with direct democracy and very high incomes.
dyk: The country is named after its ruling family, not the other way round: the Liechtensteins took their name from a castle south of Vienna, far from Vaduz.
ev: Prince Johann Adam Andreas buys the Lordship of Schellenberg
The same prince buys the County of Vaduz
Emperor Charles VI creates the Principality of Liechtenstein
Liechtenstein joins the Confederation of the Rhine and becomes sovereign
Prince Johann II abolishes the army
A new constitution shares power between prince and people

f.founder: Prince Anton Florian of Liechtenstein (principality created by Emperor Charles VI)
f.predecessor: Lordship of Schellenberg; County of Vaduz
